Nature Communications | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte that forms a weakly solvating environment, enabling preferential preemptive passivation of both electrodes. Its significance is achieving ~0 s self-extinguishing time, stable high-voltage cycling in lithium metal and lithium-ion batteries, improved rate and low-temperature performance, and an 87 °C delayed thermal runaway onset—offering a viable route to safe, high-energy batteries.
